newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Aug 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- First column in special series on achievements since 14th Communist Party Congress,
- The Liaohe oilfield, China's third largest, has improved management to avoid losses and to increase profits.
- Zhang Wule, vice-minister in charge of State Economic and Trade Commission, calls for greater efforts to reduce burden on enterprises.
- To uphold morals, 10,000 young people in Beijing, Tianjin, and Jinan offer services to local residents.
- Editorial warns children against electronic pets
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH

- The Propaganda Department forum on theory from July 30 to August 1 calls on theoreticians to focus on Jiang Zemin's speech at the Party School on May 29, to adhere to Deng Xiaoping's theory of building socialism with Chinese characteristics.
- An exhibition at the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution shows achievements of the People's Liberation Army.
- Civil Aviation Administration of China says eight new airports and three airport expansion projects will be completed this year.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Experts say shareholding reform should be important part of strategy in raising capital for oil and gas fields
- State Information Centre says lowering tax rates would benefit steady development of enterprises
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- China will become fastest nuclear power developing contry in the world, with capacity of 20,000 megawatts by 2010
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- Exports of state-owned enterprises reach $45.67 billion in first half, upo 25.3 percent from a year ago
CHINA DAILY

- Urban reforms, which are a major part of China's reform drive, have done well in last few years in establishing a socialist market system, says Zhang Haoruo, vice-minister of the State Commission for Restructuring Economic Systems.
- National conference on protecting historical relics opens in Nanchang.
- A number of newly discovered mineral deposits in southwestern China indicate good non-ferrous metal production.
- General Fu Quanyou, a member of the Central Military Commission and chief of the General Staff of the PLA, began a visit to the United States and Finland.
